key_insight: Paint-Anything teaches a model to understand 24-bit hex color values as a universal control signal for both image generation and editing. The key breakthrough is a unified way to specify exact colors without relying on custom color encodings or specialized inference tricks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of precise any-color control in AI image generation and editing. Existing methods often support only limited color palettes, require dedicated representations, or use separate procedures for different tasks.
method: Learns a shared representation that links hex color codes to visual color semantics.
Uses this representation to control object color consistently across both generation and editing workflows.
Builds on the observation that even compact language models can associate hex values with color concepts, simplifying the control pipeline.
impact: This makes color control more exact, intuitive, and practical for design-focused AI applications. For practitioners, it reduces the need for task-specific color tooling and enables a single interface for both creating and modifying colored objects.

paper_title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
paper_authors: Ji Xie, Dewei Zhou, Xinyu Huang, Zhennan Chen, Xun Wang
